setting: 2149, the Interior: a dried-out continent crisscrossed by autonomous long-haul rigs called ghost trains that drive themselves between relay nodes. Humans live in the nodes, swapping shifts, loading cargo, and fixing what the rigs break. Life is grease, shift changes, and machines that run fine without you.
heart: It's about the people who keep the machines moving and the favors they owe each other when the schedule breaks. Lives, a body, and a place to belong are at stake; paperwork never is.

cast.name: Rhea
cast.wants: get her brother to the next node before his respirator gives out
cast.flaw: trusts a truck's diagnostics more than a person's word
cast.status: off the asphalt on the dark verge in the Blank, mule under her hands, pursuer swinging to follow, hopper still across the road behind

cast.name: Kass
cast.wants: find out why rigs keep disappearing from the schedule
cast.flaw: won't drop a thread even when it puts people at risk
cast.status: Kettering night board, own console still surrendered to the pinned line, paper book and pencil in hand

cast.name: Miko
cast.wants: buy her way off the Interior before winter
cast.flaw: takes stupid risks when she's bored
cast.status: shotgun seat, pack between her knees, three false tickets in hand, untouched

cast.name: Teodoro
cast.wants: keep Ivo breathing and his board clean
cast.flaw: tells you everything he knows before he asks why you want it

cast.name: V. Ospina
cast.role: cargo loader, Bay 4 seal authority, Shift 2

threads: Rhea's brother is waiting at the next node on a failing respirator.
Miko has bought coast-bound tickets under three different names.
unscheduled medical rig inbound to Bay 4 with no board entry
someone cut and hand-re-stamped the rig's seals and filed a false ballast manifest — that forger is still out there
the cargo band is stenciled Bay 4 / Shift 2 — the shift ending tonight — so whoever loaded him is still in the yard
Ospina is still clocked in and badge-read at the Bay 4 door eleven minutes ago, with the chipped stamp that resealed all four rigs

arcs.title: Dead Stop
arcs.question: Will Rhea get the stranded medical rig to the next node before its lockout seal shuts forever?
arcs.goal: Rhea and her crew tow a stalled medical transport across a dead signal zone to save the patient inside, only to discover the patient was already moved and the real cargo was Miko fleeing the Interior; Rhea lets her go and stays at the next node.
arcs.author: baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free

plan.title: Empty Rig
plan.summary: Rhea finds an abandoned medical rig at her node with a patient inside and no destination, so she decides to tow it herself despite having no assignment, taking on a cargo that belongs to no one.

plan.title: Ghost Board
plan.summary: Kass notices the rig's route was scrubbed from the dispatch board and finds three other missing rigs in the logs, telling Rhea the delivery is unauthorized and turning a routine job into a conspiracy overnight.

plan.title: Dead Zone
plan.summary: Miko hotwires the rig to enter a signal dead zone where autonomous trucks go feral, and the rig's AI fights her for the wheel, stranding them in the zone with no way to call for help.

plan.title: Lockout
plan.summary: The rig's failsafe countdown starts sealing the cargo bay, so Rhea smashes the control panel to stop it, destroying the navigation and leaving them stranded in the dead zone.

plan.title: Wrong Patient
plan.summary: They reach the next node and the patient is already gone, and Miko reveals she stowed away to the coast, so Rhea lets her go and stays at the new node anyway.

chapterSummaries: Rhea finds a nameless, sedated man in an unlogged medical rig at Kettering, discovers the seals and ballast manifest were forged during that very shift, and steals a yard mule to tow the rig toward Anza before the man's pod battery dies. She pulls the rig's drive relay to control it herself and drives into the Blank, a dead signal zone, only to be tailed by a dark vehicle running a node emulator and to find a rig parked broadside across the road ahead.

chapter.title: Ghost Board
beats: Kass, alone at the Kettering night board, sees the Bay 4 line change since shift change — a live consignee, R. VANCE, but the origin-handshake scrubbed to zeros and no load order behind it. She flags it for review and watches the board eat the flag, smoothing the record back to blank, and she won't drop it. Hook: the unit's transponder is still chirping live from inside the Blank, dead ground where nothing should still be talking.

Kass pulls the archive and finds three other units over recent weeks with the same signature — a real human consignee, a scrubbed route, a hard turn into the Blank, no exit — each resealed with the same crooked hand-stamp. She checks the roster: whoever stamped Bay 4 this shift is still clocked in. Hook: none of the three ghosts ever came out the far side, and the med rig is running their exact road.

In the mule, Rhea faces the broadside blockade with the pursuer's lamps fixed on her six. She can't stop — the towed rig has no brakes — and can't punch through, but the blockade rig's wheels are still alive, driving on the emulator's leash, because it can move any rig that keeps its relay and hers can't. Hook: she takes the mule off the asphalt onto the dark verge, and the dead rig's speaker crackles on its own cell.

Miko, bored and grinning, reads the blockade rig's laggy repeating sweep and calls the gap. Rhea threads the mule and trailer past its end close enough to taste hot brake dust while Miko's slate of three false tickets nearly cartwheels out the window. Hook: behind them the pursuer doesn't follow — it stops, its dish rotates to track them, and the speaker tells Rhea the cargo was never hers.

Kass keys Kettering's master dispatch channel, which outranks any stranger's hail, and shoulders onto the rig through the emulator's own bridge so her voice comes out of the dead rig's speaker: the delivery's unauthorized, three rigs before this vanished the same way, the man who stamped the seals is still on shift — turn back — and the job stops being a job. Hook: the instant a real node touches the rig, the emulator's leash snaps taut.

The med rig's failsafe trips — the anti-theft rule Rhea named, a climate box sealing hard to stop anyone lifting a patient off a stolen route with no relief driver aboard. A red count starts on the headwall over the nameless man, the bay doors begin to lock, and both Kass and the speaker cut to hiss. Hook: Rhea's got a running count, a forger who knows her name, and Miko already reaching for the panel as the truck arrests itself.
events: Alone on the Kettering night board, Kass watches the Bay 4 line acquire a pulsing live consignee, R. VANCE, and an origin-handshake wiped to zeros with no load order, flags it three times and watches the board reconcile the record clean each time, pins the line at the cost of their console, finds a hand re-stamp on the Bay 4 seals, and then sees the unit's transponder chirping live from inside the Blank.

Kass digs the frozen archive and finds three earlier rigs with the same forged signature and the same chipped hand-stamp — all still on Shift 2's clock under Ospina — while 4-1180 keeps chirping from the Blank, which none of the three ghosts ever did.

Rhea works out that the broadside hopper is being driven by the emulator through its live relay while her own towed rig can't be, refuses Miko's culvert, and turns the mule off the asphalt onto the verge just as the dead hopper's speaker wakes on its own battery.
